summary: Redwood and Nova DataWorks reviewed the POC acceptance runbook, defined go/no-go thresholds across latency, cost, and quality, and agreed on benchmark schedule and reporting format. Action items assigned for harness delivery and trace export.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Jenna (Redwood SE), Marco (Redwood SE), Lena (Nova ML), Marcus (Infra), Priya (PM)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, really quick agenda - run through the acceptance runbook, confirm success metrics, sizing, and schedule the benchmark run.
[00:14] Lena: Yep sounds good. We have a lot riding on the POC so want the criteria to be very explicit.
[00:22] Jenna: Totally, we'll walk through the pass/fail rubric and the reporting artifact you'll get back. Note up front that some names may be off in the transcript - product names like Redwood Dedicated sometimes come out as "read would" in auto transcripts.
[00:40] Marcus: Quick context - current traffic is about 120 requests per second at peak, average prompt length 420 tokens, typical completion length 110 tokens. Latency SLO we're targeting is p95 under 250ms for the user-facing path.
[01:05] Marco: Good, that's helpful. For the benchmark we recommend running a 2-hour synthetic replay at 1.2x peak, plus a few long-tail tests for spikes.
[01:20] Priya: For acceptance, we want both quantitative and qualitative checks. Quant: latency, availability, cost-per-1k-tokens. Qual: human eval on a 200 prompt sample.
[01:38] Jenna: Exactly. Our proposed go/no-go thresholds:
- Latency: p95 < 200ms for hosted baseline; for private/dedicated acceptable threshold is p95 < 300ms but with cost offset defined.
- Availability: >= 99.5% during run.
- Quality: human-rated accuracy >= 85% on the evaluation set OR no regression >5% vs your current baseline.
- Cost: projected steady-state cost <= $X per 1k tokens (we'll calculate using your traces) OR < 20% increase vs current infra spend for generation.
[02:15] Lena: The 85% is fine as a starting point; we may tighten depending on stakeholder signoff. Also want a ranking of failure modes — e.g., if latency fails but quality > baseline, do we still pass?
[02:34] Samir: Good question — we use a weighted rubric in the runbook. Example: quality 40%, latency 30%, cost 20%, availability 10%. Passing requires weighted score >= 70%. We'll share the exact scoring sheet.
[02:52] Marcus: How do you handle fallback behavior? If Dedicated nodes run out, will you automatically route to a cheaper model? We need deterministic behavior for the test.
[03:08] Marco: For the POC we can lock routing policies. We'll provide a run with "strict" routing (no cross-model fallback) and an additional run with fallback enabled to show graceful degradation. The runbook documents both and flags which run is used for acceptance.
[03:30] Priya: On reporting format — we prefer a CSV with these columns: timestamp, request_id, prompt_id, model_variant, latency_ms, status_code, token_count_in, token_count_out, cost_estimate_usd. Plus a one-page executive summary PDF.
[03:55] Jenna: We'll produce exactly that schema and include per-route percentiles, histograms, and a cost projection sheet (Google Sheets link).
[04:10] Lena: For quality eval, we'll do a blind human rating. Do you provide an annotation interface or do we handle it?
[04:20] Jenna: We can provide an export template and a simple web UI for blind review. For the first pass you can use your internal raters and upload CSV. We'll then compute aggregate scores and compare to baseline.
[04:36] Marcus: Sizing question — is 120 qps with 530 tokens total (in+out) realistic for your harness? We need to ensure the harness replicates our connection behavior, prefix cache hits, and KV cache patterns.
[04:52] Marco: Yes, we'll parameterize prefix caching and kv-cache hit rates. Please include traces that show typical session lengths and cache priming.
[05:05] Samir: On timeline — proposed: Redwood shares harness + runbook by 2026-02-18, you share traces by 2026-02-19, we run internal dry-run 2026-02-20, official benchmark week of 2026-02-22, follow-up review 2026-02-26. Any blockers?
[05:28] Lena: Sounds reasonable. Procurement cycles aside, the legal team needs to see minimal data residency language but we're fine with anonymized traces.
[05:40] Priya: Can we also get a sample pass/fail report template? We want to know what a failing report looks like so stakeholders can interpret it.
[05:50] Jenna: Yes — pass/fail will include: scoring table, percentile latency plots, cost delta vs baseline, top-10 failure reasons (e.g., timeouts, long-tail token blowups), and a recommendation section. We'll attach a mock failing and mock passing example.
[06:12] Marcus: About the cost metric — how do you estimate cost across model variants and quantization?
[06:20] Marco: We run the same traces against each model variant and record tokens and GPU time; our cost sheet uses Redwood unit costs for hosted and an estimated cost-per-GPU-hour for private. We also include quantized model variants (8-bit/4-bit) and approximate quality deltas.
[06:39] Lena: If the quality delta between quantized and full precision is >7%, we won't accept quantized for customer-facing. That will be in the acceptance criteria.
[06:48] Samir: Noted. We'll add a hard gate: if quality regression >7% on the human-eval set, quantized variant is disqualified from the production recommendation.
[07:00] Priya: What about monitoring and observability during the POC? We need token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency breakdown in near real-time.
[07:12] Jenna: Redwood Console will provide dashboards; for the POC we can give a 48-hour retention export and CSV snapshots. For the final product you can opt into longer retention.
[07:25] Marcus: Security question — will the benchmark harness send any PII? We will scrub traces but want to ensure the runbook calls out sanitization.
[07:33] Marco: We include a sanitization step in the runbook and a checklist for trace exports. We recommend you run the scrub locally before upload.
[07:45] Lena: Ok good. One more on acceptance: do we need to hit both latency and cost thresholds or can one offset the other?
[07:55] Samir: That's where the weighted scoring comes in. If latency misses but quality and cost are strong, you can still pass if weighted score >= 70%. However, critical failures (availability < 98% or quality < 65%) auto-fail.
[08:15] Priya: For the human eval set — we will seed 200 examples drawn from 7 days of traffic and stratified by prompt type. Should the POC also include adversarial prompts?
[08:27] Jenna: Yes, include a 20-example adversarial set to stress guardrails and hallucination checks; those examples get flagged separately in the report.
[08:37] Marcus: Operational acceptance — do we expect a handoff doc for Dedicated? Like runbook for scaling, autoscale triggers, and alerting?
[08:47] Marco: We'll deliver a handoff packet with autoscale thresholds, recommended GPU configs, and runbook playbooks. That's part of the deliverables.
[09:00] Samir: Quick recap of deliverables: harness + runbook, reporting template + CSV schema, pass/fail scoring sheet, mock pass/fail reports, and the cost projection sheet. Action items on the doc reflect that.
[09:18] Lena: I have one stakeholder ask — legal will want an SLA trigger for sell-off. If POC fails, what are remediation options? Do you offer extended trial or rollback to previous setup?
[09:31] Samir: We typically offer a remediation period — e.g., 2 weeks to iterate on configuration and rerun benchmarks once. We'll put that remediation window in the runbook and commercial sheet.
[09:45] Priya: For the benchmark runs, will you provide raw logs so we can run our own analysis offline?
[09:53] Jenna: Yes, raw logs (anonymized) and aggregated reports. We also provide the harness repo so you can replay locally.
[10:02] Marcus: Anything else on telemetry? We need token-level attribution by route and by model version.
[10:10] Marco: We'll include token breakdown in the CSV schema and a per-request cost column.
[10:17] Samir: Okay, let's talk about the acceptance thresholds in plain language and I'll capture them on the call.
[10:23] Jenna: I'll read the final list — 1) Quality: human eval >=85% or no regression >5% vs baseline. 2) Latency: p95 <200ms hosted / <300ms dedicated. 3) Availability >=99.5%. 4) Cost: projected steady-state cost within agreed delta (TBD - we'll compute). 5) Critical gates: availability >=98%, quality >=65% (auto-fail if below). Weighted pass threshold 70%.
[10:54] Lena: Sounds good. Make sure the cost calculation assumptions are documented.
[11:02] Marco: We'll annotate the cost sheet with assumptions: tokenization method, avg tokens per request, GPU-hour price, and amortized overhead.
[11:12] Priya: For the reporting cadence, we want an interim quick-check 24 hours after the run and a final report within 3 business days.
[11:22] Samir: Agreed. Interim export + daily dashboard, final report within 72 hours.
[11:30] Lena: Any concerns about noisy tails? Our traffic has periodic spikes linked to marketing events.
[11:38] Jenna: We'll run a tail-resilience test consisting of several burst patterns at 2x and 4x peak for 10 minutes each and include that in the results. Those are separate from the standard acceptance run but informative.
[11:55] Marcus: Ok great. Anything else?
[12:00] Priya: Please include a short one-page FAQ for internal stakeholders explaining acceptance logic.
[12:06] Samir: Will do.
[12:12] Lena: Thanks everyone.
[12:15] Samir: Thanks, talk soon.

End transcript.
